summary: The root ثري (thry) primarily denotes abundance, especially of wealth and possessions. It signifies being rich, opulent, or having a large amount of something.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: ثَرِيَتِ الأَرْضُ , aor. ثَرَىَ, inf. n. ثَرٌى, The earth, or land, became moist and soft, after drought and dryness: (M, K:) or became watered by rain that penetrated to its moistness. (Msb.) See also the same form of the verb in the first paragraph of art. ثرو, in six places.

ثرّى ثر ثرى ثري ثريي, (T, S, M, K,) inf. n. تَثْرِيَةٌ, (S, K,) He moistened (T, S, M, K) a place, (T,) or earth, or the ground, or dust, (M, K,) and سَوِيق [or meal of parched barley or wheat], (S, TA,) and any other thing: (TA:) he sprinkled a place: (S, K:) he poured water upon, and then stirred about, and mixed up, [the preparation of milk termed] أَقِط, (M, K,) and سَوِيق.

اثرى أثر أثرى أثري أثريي إثر إثري اثرى اثري ثري It (rain) moistened the earth. (S.) أَثْرَتِ الأَرْضُ The land, or earth, had much moisture; became abundant in moisture: (S, M, Msb, K:) or it became compact with moisture. (AHn, M.) [See also مُثْرٍ.]

ثَرًى ثر ثرى ثري ثريي Moisture; humidity; (S, M, K;) of the earth: (S, Msb:) and moist earth; (S, M, Msb, K;) تُرَاب that is not moist is not called ثَرًى; (Msb;) or such as, when moistened, does not become cohesive mud or clay; (M, K;) as also [an epithet used as a subst.]: (AO, T, * K, TA: [in the CK, erroneously, ثَرَياء:]) and the earth;; (M, K) مَا تَحْتَ الثَّرَي, in the Kur [xx.

[ ثَرٍ ثر, fem. ثَرِيَةٌ, Moist; humid. ] You say أَرْضٌ ثَرِيَةٌ, (M, Msb,) like عَمِيَةٌ, (Msb,) or, like غَنِيَّةٌ, (K, [but this is anomalous, as part. n. of ثَرِيَت,]) and, (Msb, K,) Earth, or land, that has become moist and soft, after drought and dryness: (M, K:) or watered by rain that has penetrated to its moistness: (Msb:) or the last, land of just, or moderate, moisture: (AHn, M:) or moist land; (T, S, M;) and so the first.
ثَرِىٌّ ثر ثرى ثري ثريي, fem. ثَرِيَّةٌ: see ثَرٍ, in two places: and see also art. ثرو.
ثَرْيَآءُ ثريآء: see ثَرٍ: and see also ثَرًى.
ثُرَيَّا ثري ثريا: see art. ثرو.
: see ثَرًى: and see also art. ثرو.

[ مُثْرٍ مثر, fem. مُثْرِيَةٌ, part. n. of 4, q. v.] أَرْضٌ مُثْرِيَةٌ [is explained as meaning] Land of which the earth has not become dry. (T, TA.) See also ثَرًى, last two sentences. And see art. ثرو.
مَثْرِىُّ مثرى مثري a pass. part. n. having no verb; used as an intensive epithet in the phrase ثَرًى مَثْرِىٌّ [ Very moist earth ]. (M.) See also art. ثرو.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
